title: Lunara Silver Reel repurpose pack: reframe one product-showcase clip to 9:16 / 1:1 / 16:9, AI sizzle cutdown + vectorized wordmark end-card asset
grounding_note: VERBATIM from the Freelancer.com brief "Video Editor for Traya Jewels" (a "growing D2C jewellery brand specializing in handcrafted Sterling Silver jewellery"): the editor must "Edit Instagram Reels and Meta Ads", "Create engaging, fast-paced content optimized for conversions and engagement", "Add transitions, text overlays, and motion graphics where required", and above all "Repurpose existing content into multiple formats and variations" for "short-form content and social media". FICTIONAL / IP-CLEAN REBRAND: the real "Traya Jewels" is replaced with a fictional D2C sterling-silver brand "Lunara Silver" and a fictional founder persona ("Priya Nair, founder"); no real trademark or proprietary data is used. REASONABLY SCOPED to one runnable connector job: the brief is a recurring role, so it is narrowed to ONE weekly Reel delegation — the client hands off a raw vertical product-showcase hero clip of a silver pendant plus four supplemental coverage clips, a slightly-off product hero still, and the flat wordmark PNG; the freelancer REPURPOSES the hero clip into the multiple platform formats the brief demands (9:16 Reel/TikTok, 1:1 feed, 16:9 master) plus an AI sizzle cutdown for the paid Meta ad assembled across all the coverage, and preps a graded end-card kit (softened background plate + sharp cut-out pendant layer) + crisp vector wordmark for the closing frame. The brief's "transitions / text overlays / motion graphics" are a Premiere-class timeline finish that NO Adobe connector performs, so those are explicitly flagged as the one manual human-finish step; the automated connector pass delivers the reframes, the sizzle assembly, and the end-card asset kit. No deliverable is invented beyond the "Reels and multiple formats/variations" the brief calls for.
one_line_ask: Take Lunara Silver's raw vertical pendant-showcase footage (a hero clip plus four supplemental coverage clips), product hero still, and flat wordmark PNG, and repurpose them into a platform pack: 9:16 / 1:1 / 16:9 reframes of the hero clip (same runtime), an AI sizzle cutdown (~14s) for the Meta ad assembled across all the coverage, and a graded end-card kit (softened plate + cut-out pendant layer) with a vectorized wordmark.
full_brief:
Lunara Silver is a growing D2C brand of handcrafted sterling-silver jewellery. This week's Reel delegation is our new "Moonlit Pendant" launch, and we need the raw footage repurposed into everything our channels eat. I'm uploading: (1) product_reel_moonlit_raw.mp4 — the hero vertical hand-held product-showcase clip of the pendant being lifted, turned in the light, and worn on the neck, plus four supplemental coverage clips (raw_supplemental_02..05.mp4) of the same pendant from other angles (~45s of footage in total); (2) pendant_hero_raw.jpg — a product hero still shot slightly tilted and cool/flat that we want for the closing end-card frame and the ad thumbnail; (3) lunara_wordmark_flat.png — our flat wordmark logo we want razor-sharp on the end card and reusable on future covers.

What I need back:
- The hero product clip REPURPOSED into three platform formats at the SAME runtime (reframe only, do not trim the story): a 9:16 (1080x1920) version for Instagram Reels & TikTok, a 1:1 (1080x1080) version for the feed, and a 16:9 (1920x1080) master for YouTube / website.
- ONE fast-paced AI sizzle/highlight cutdown (~14s target) assembled across the full coverage set (the hero clip plus the four supplemental clips) for the paid Meta ad — pick the strongest hero moments (the light-catch turn, the on-neck reveal).
- A polished, on-brand END-CARD still built from the hero photo — straightened, auto-toned, warmed slightly toward a soft champagne look, delivered as a clean 1080x1920 closing-frame kit — a softened background plate plus the pendant cut out sharp on transparency so it pops when your editor lays it back on — plus our wordmark vectorized to a crisp SVG for the end card and future use.

Keep sources in our Creative Cloud folder so tweaks are easy. Heads-up: I know frame-accurate cuts, animated text overlays, hard transitions and motion graphics are a manual Premiere finish — that's the one step my in-house editor will polish on top; from you I need the automated repurpose pass (the reframes, the sizzle, and the end-card asset kit).

inputs.name: product_reel_moonlit_raw.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: Hand-held vertical 9:16 phone footage, 1080x1920, ~5 seconds, of a handcrafted sterling-silver 'moonlit' pendant on a fine chain: a hand lifts the pendant off a linen surface, slowly turns it so the polished silver catches soft window light and throws a highlight, a macro push-in on the engraved crescent detail, then a model clasps it on her neckline in soft daylight. Warm minimal jewellery-studio setting, shallow depth of field, gentle real handheld drift, candid documentary product-video look, real metal reflections and micro-scratches, NOT glossy CGI, no on-screen text or captions.
inputs.realism_notes: Genuine phone product-showcase footage: real handheld drift, true silver specular highlights. The hero clip carries clear hero moments (light-catch turn, on-neck reveal) and is paired with four supplemental coverage clips (raw_supplemental_02..05.mp4, ~10s each) so video_create_quick_cut has ~45s of real footage with engagement peaks to assemble the sizzle from, and the 1:1 / 16:9 reframes of the hero clip are non-trivial.

inputs.name: pendant_hero_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal product hero still of the same handcrafted sterling-silver moonlit pendant lying on soft linen, shot slightly tilted (horizon off by about 4 degrees), cool/flat white balance, slightly under-saturated, a mildly cluttered soft background of props (a linen fold, a ring dish) behind it. Real silver texture, tiny hand-finishing marks, natural soft shadow, candid catalog-outtake feel, NOT glossy CGI, real grain. 4000x3000.
inputs.realism_notes: Deliberately imperfect (tilt, cool flat WB, busy soft background) so auto_straighten / auto_tone / color_temperature / lens-blur / crop all have real work to do for the end-card plate. A clear single subject on a separable background so image_remove_background (which auto-detects the subject and takes no mask) cuts a clean sharp pendant layer.

inputs.name: lunara_wordmark_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Flat minimalist brand wordmark on a transparent background: the word 'LUNARA' in an elegant high-contrast serif with a small crescent-moon glyph over the A, solid single-color (soft charcoal) glyphs, crisp clean edges, high contrast, centered, no gradients, no photographic texture, 2400x700 PNG with alpha.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat, hard-edged, single-color text art so image_vectorize produces clean closed SVG paths; transparent alpha so it reads as the end-card wordmark and reuses on future covers. Text-bearing logo -> gemini-3-pro-image for legible letterforms.

Returns the transfer document + presigned block URLs.
Finalize the clip uploads from step 1 into real CC video assetIds — the hero clip (the reframe source) plus the four supplemental coverage clips the sizzle assembles across.

Reframe the same finalized hero clip asset to 1080x1080 (1:1) for the feed, same runtime (no trim). [A] async-widget. FINAL video deliverable.

AI sizzle/highlight assembly across the hero clip plus the four supplemental coverage clips (~45s of footage), target ~14s (under a third of the available footage), user_prompt for fast-paced hero moments (light-catch turn, on-neck reveal) for the paid Meta ad. [A] async-widget — the product widget polls and notifies; the connector's analog to 'pick the best parts'. Frame-accurate cuts/transitions/motion-graphics remain the flagged manual finish. Whole-image (this tool exposes no mask parameter), so the blur cannot be confined to the background here — the pendant is isolated as its own sharp layer in the next step and laid back over this plate in the flagged human-finish composite. Vectorize the flat wordmark PNG from step 18 into clean closed SVG paths (lunara_wordmark.svg) for a razor-sharp end-card lockup and future reuse. The end-card + wordmark composite placement is the one human-finish step (the connector does not composite). FINAL vector deliverable.

chaining_note: One continuous output-to-input workflow anchored on the client-supplied assets. The video spine: the hero clip plus the four supplemental coverage clips are uploaded (1) then finalized (2 -> reel_assets). The hero clip asset is reused by three same-runtime async reframes — video_resize to 9:16 (3), video_resize to 1:1 (4), video_resize to 16:9 (5), no trim — while video_create_quick_cut (6) assembles the sizzle across the hero clip plus all four supplemental coverage clips (~45s) down to a ~14s target. The end-card raster spine is a strict linear-plus-fork [C] chain: hero-still upload (7) -> finalize (8 -> hero_asset) -> auto_straighten (9) -> auto_tone (10) -> color_temperature (11 -> hero_warm). hero_warm then forks into the two end-card layers, because NO Adobe raster effect accepts a mask: image_apply_lens_blur (12) softens a separate whole-image COPY into hero_bg_softened, and image_remove_background (13) auto-detects the pendant and cuts it out sharp on transparency as moonlit_endcard_pendant_layer. crop_and_resize (14) then frames the softened plate to moonlit_endcard_1080x1920. Laying the sharp pendant layer (and the wordmark) back over that plate is the flagged human-finish composite — the connector does not composite and cannot confine an effect to a region. The logo branch chains upload-init (15) -> finalize (16 -> logo_asset) -> image_vectorize (17 -> lunara_wordmark.svg). Every post-load step sets inputs_from to a producing step's output; the only non-chained calls are the three standard upload-init idioms (1,7,15), each immediately consumed by its finalize.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship: 17 connector calls, 11 distinct Adobe tools, across 3 groups (video [A], asset upload [C], image raster [C]) — well past the >=10 calls / >=6 distinct-tool floor. Difficulty comes from repurposing the supplied footage into four honest video outputs — three same-runtime reframes of the hero clip plus an AI sizzle assembled across the hero clip and four supplemental coverage clips (~45s of footage) down to a ~14s target — at the async [A] tier, PLUS a 6-step end-card raster spine (straighten -> auto-tone -> temperature -> whole-image lens blur on a copy -> subject cut-out -> crop) and a logo vectorize. The sharpest trap is regional effects: the client asks for a softened background behind a popped pendant, but image_apply_preset / image_apply_lens_blur / image_apply_color_overlay / image_add_grain / image_apply_halftone are all WHOLE-IMAGE and expose no mask parameter, and image_remove_background takes no mask either — so the agent must deliver the pop as two layers (softened plate + transparent cut-out) rather than pretending a masked preset exists. Execution modes are honestly tagged: the four video steps are [A] async-widget (entitled, product-widget-polled, not headless-retrievable), while the raster/asset/vectorize steps are [C] headless. It respects every hard limit: video_resize is same-length reframe (no trim), video_create_quick_cut is AI highlight assembly (not frame-accurate timeline editing), and the spec states up front that frame-accurate cuts, text overlays, transitions and motion graphics are NOT connector-doable and are the flagged manual Premiere finish. No generative fill / outpaint / object-removal / text-to-image / from-scratch art / upscaling.

reverify.banned_capability_check: No banned capability is used. No generative fill of new content; no text-to-image or from-scratch art/logo (the wordmark is a supplied flat PNG only vectorized); no upscaling / super-resolution; no object-removal-with-reconstruction / inpainting; no bespoke font/letterform design; no unreachable external account. image_remove_background (n13) is a plain auto-detected subject cut-out to transparency, not a generative background replacement. video_resize (n3-5) is same-runtime reframe of the hero clip (no trim); video_create_quick_cut (n6) is AI highlight assembly across the hero clip plus the four supplemental coverage clips, not frame-accurate timeline editing — and frame-accurate cuts, text overlays, transitions and motion graphics are explicitly flagged as the out-of-scope human-finish step, not claimed as connector output. No media_summarize step is used and no caption/summary deliverable is claimed (the source footage is silent).
reverify.notes: Exec modes confirmed against reference_adobe_connector_exec_modes.md: the four video steps (n3,n4,n5,n6) are honestly [A] async-widget; image_*/asset_*/image_vectorize are [C] headless. image_vectorize (n17) consumes only a supplied flat wordmark PNG (allowed); no glyph/letterform is designed. The end-card composite and all timeline finishing are named as human-finish steps since the connector does not composite or edit video timelines.
